figures.caption: Fig. 1: SCNB breaks semantic color plausibility. UE generated from PAChroma suppresses chroma magnitude but can leave gray-but-natural outputs, whereas SCNB induces content-inconsistent colors even under restricted settings.
Fig. 9: Improved transferability via ensemble-crafted UE. Rows correspond to surrogate ensembles used for crafting SCNB and columns to attack (evaluation) models.
TABLE II: Transferability with ensemble-crafted UE. CaCDD increases on unseen target models under ϵ=32/255 when SCNB is crafted using multiple surrogate colorizers.
Fig. 2: Uncolorable Example generated from SCNB inducing implausible color. Each image is shown with its SSIM between the inputs and CaCDD score.
Fig. 10: Illustrative idea of CaCDD components. H(p) evaluates the inconsistency of hue directions, wheras D(p) measures the out-of-distribution distance to the GMM.
Fig. 5: Semantic prior construction. Open-vocabulary tags and masks are used to collect ab channels of CIELAB per class and fit class-conditional GMM priors.
Fig. 6: Region-wise CaCDD visualization. Low CaCDD indicates semantically plausible colors, whereas high CaCDD indicates content-inconsistent colors.
Fig. 12: CaCDD show weak correlation to conventional metrics. Scatter plots of CaCDD vs. CF, SSIM, and PSNR evaluated with outputs of BigColor, DDColor, and DeOldify.

TABLE V: SCNB vs. PAChroma on ImageNet (mean over 80 runs: 40 images × 2 seeds). We report CF and CaCDD on unprotected/protected outputs, and CaCDD after post-processing (JPEG Q=75/50, RRC). SCNB increases CaCDD, while PAChroma reduces CF.
TABLE I: ImageNet transferability and robustness (BigColor as source). “Source” crafts the perturbation and “Attack” is used for evaluation (white-box: Source=Attack). ϵ=32/255.
